PixelForge does not normally store complete payment card numbers or card security codes in its own application database. Sensitive payment information is processed by authorized payment service providers.

Depending on the payment arrangement, an amount may initially be reserved on the customer's card before the transaction is finalized. The timing of the final charge depends on the payment provider and the applicable checkout terms.

If a card payment is declined, customers should verify their payment details, available funds, and any authentication requests from their bank.

## Swish Payments

When Swish is available at checkout, customers can complete payment using the Swish application and the verification method required by their bank.

The payment must be approved within the time allowed by the payment provider. If the customer closes the payment process before completing authorization, the order may remain unpaid or fail to be confirmed.

Customers should verify the payment status before attempting to place the same order again, particularly if their banking application indicates that money has already been transferred.

## Invoice Payments

Invoice payments may be offered through an external payment provider. Customers choosing this option may be required to provide additional identification information and undergo a credit assessment.

The payment provider determines whether invoice payment is available and communicates the applicable payment deadline and terms.

Customers are responsible for paying invoices by the specified due date. Late payment fees or interest may apply according to the provider's terms and applicable legislation.

For information about invoice documentation and payment corrections, see Invoices & Receipts.

## Instalment Payments

Eligible customers may be offered instalment plans that allow a purchase to be paid over several months.

Instalment plans are provided by external financial service partners and may involve interest, administrative fees, or other credit costs.

The total cost of credit, payment schedule, and applicable conditions must be presented before the customer enters into the agreement.

Customers should review these terms carefully. PixelForge does not independently approve credit applications or determine the payment provider's credit decisions.

## Payment Confirmation

After a successful purchase, PixelForge sends an order confirmation to the email address supplied during checkout.

An order confirmation normally includes the order number, purchased products, total price, selected delivery method, and payment status when available.

Receiving an order confirmation does not necessarily mean that the products have already been dispatched. Orders may still require payment verification, stock confirmation, or warehouse processing.

## Failed or Interrupted Payments

A payment may fail because of insufficient funds, incorrect payment details, expired cards, authentication problems, or temporary interruptions at the payment provider.

Customers who encounter a payment error should first check whether the transaction appears in their bank or payment application.

If the payment appears to have been completed but no order confirmation arrives, customers should contact PixelForge support before placing another order. This helps prevent duplicate purchases.

## Changing a Payment Method

Once an order has been confirmed, changing the payment method may not be possible. Customers should contact support if they need assistance with a payment-related issue.

For some orders, cancellation and placement of a new order may be necessary, provided the original order has not already been dispatched.

## Refunds and Payment Providers

Refunds are normally returned through the original payment method. For card payments, banks may require several business days to complete the transaction.

Invoice and instalment refunds may involve adjustments to an outstanding balance or reimbursement of payments already made.

For complete refund procedures, see Refund Process. For information about payment protection and fraud prevention, consult Payment Security.

title: Invoices & Receipts
description: Information about order receipts, invoices, payment deadlines, VAT details, and corrections to payment documents.
content:
# Invoices & Receipts

PixelForge provides purchase documentation to help customers keep track of payments, verify order details, and manage warranty or return requests.

The type of documentation available depends on the payment method used and whether the purchase was completed as a private consumer or on behalf of a business.

## Order Confirmations

After a customer completes checkout, PixelForge normally sends an order confirmation to the email address provided during the purchase.

The confirmation includes the order number, purchased products, quantities, prices, applicable discounts, delivery charges, and the total order value.

An order confirmation records the details of a purchase but is not always equivalent to a final payment receipt or an invoice.

Customers should retain the confirmation because the order number is useful when contacting support, requesting a return, or submitting a warranty claim.

## Payment Receipts

Customers who complete payment using a card or Swish may receive a digital payment receipt or transaction confirmation.

Receipts normally identify the purchase amount, transaction date, payment method, and relevant order reference.

Depending on the payment provider, the payment confirmation may be delivered separately from the PixelForge order confirmation.

Customers should check their email inbox and spam folder if expected documentation does not arrive.

## Invoice Purchases

When invoice payment is selected, the invoice is normally issued and administered by the external payment provider.

The invoice includes the payment amount, due date, payment instructions, and any applicable reference number.

Customers must follow the payment instructions provided on the invoice rather than transferring money directly to PixelForge unless explicitly instructed to do so.

Questions about invoice due dates, payment registration, or instalment arrangements may need to be handled by the payment provider.

## Invoice Payment Deadlines

The payment deadline depends on the invoice provider and the terms accepted during checkout. A common invoice period may be 14 or 30 days, but customers must follow the date stated on their individual invoice.

If an invoice is not paid by the due date, reminder fees, interest, or other charges may apply according to the provider's terms and applicable law.

Customers who believe an invoice is incorrect should contact the payment provider and PixelForge support as soon as possible rather than ignoring the payment request.

## VAT and Price Information

Product prices shown to private consumers in the PixelForge store include applicable Swedish VAT unless otherwise stated.

Purchase documentation identifies the relevant amounts and tax information according to the type of transaction and applicable invoicing requirements.

The standard Swedish VAT rate for most gaming hardware and computer accessories is 25 percent.

Business customers who require specific invoicing information should ensure that accurate company details are supplied during checkout.

## Correcting Invoice Information

Customers who discover an incorrect name, billing address, or other detail on their purchase documentation should contact PixelForge support.

Some corrections may be possible before an invoice has been finalized. Other changes may require the payment provider to issue corrected documentation.

PixelForge cannot guarantee that all invoice details can be changed after a completed transaction, particularly when legal accounting requirements apply.

## Receipts for Guest Purchases

Customers do not need a registered PixelForge account to receive purchase documentation when guest checkout is available.

Order confirmations and payment information are sent to the email address provided during checkout.

Customers who lose their confirmation may contact support with information that helps identify the purchase, such as the approximate purchase date and email address used.

For security reasons, support may require identity verification before sharing sensitive transaction information.

## Documentation for Returns and Warranty Claims

An order confirmation, receipt, invoice, or other reliable proof of purchase can help establish when and where a product was purchased.

Customers are encouraged to retain purchase documentation throughout the expected product lifetime.

A missing paper receipt does not automatically remove statutory consumer rights when the purchase can be demonstrated through other evidence.

For warranty conditions, see Warranty Policy. For return procedures, consult Return Policy.

## Credit Notes and Refund Adjustments

When a purchase is cancelled or refunded, an invoice provider may issue a credit note or adjust the outstanding invoice balance.

If a customer has already paid an invoice, the payment provider may arrange reimbursement according to its procedures.

Customers should not assume that an invoice has been cancelled until the payment provider confirms the adjustment.

For more information about refund processing, see Refund Process.

## Accounting and Record Retention

PixelForge retains accounting information as required by Swedish bookkeeping legislation. Certain accounting records generally need to be preserved for seven years.

This means that some transaction information may remain stored even after a customer requests account deletion.

For details about personal data retention and individual rights, consult Personal Data & GDPR.

title: Payment Security
description: Learn how PixelForge protects payment transactions, handles suspicious activity, and helps customers avoid payment fraud.
content:
# Payment Security

PixelForge aims to provide a secure shopping environment for customers purchasing gaming hardware and accessories. Payment security involves protecting sensitive information, verifying transactions, preventing unauthorized purchases, and helping customers recognize potential fraud.

PixelForge works with external payment service providers to process transactions using established security technologies and appropriate authentication procedures.

## Secure Connections

The PixelForge website uses HTTPS connections to protect information transmitted between customers' browsers and the website.

HTTPS uses encryption to reduce the risk of unauthorized parties reading or modifying information while it travels across a network.

Customers should verify that they are visiting the correct PixelForge website before entering account or payment information.

A secure connection is an important protection, but it does not guarantee that every website displaying a lock symbol is trustworthy. Customers should also check the website address carefully.

## Payment Service Providers

Card payments and other financial transactions are processed through external payment providers.

PixelForge does not normally store complete card numbers, card security codes, or online banking credentials in its own application database.

Payment providers are responsible for implementing the security controls applicable to their services, including relevant payment industry requirements.

PixelForge receives the transaction information necessary to administer purchases, confirm payments, and process refunds.

## Strong Customer Authentication

Certain online payments require strong customer authentication under applicable European payment regulations.

Customers may be asked to confirm a payment through their banking application, a one-time verification procedure, or another authentication method supported by their payment provider.

These additional steps help reduce the risk of unauthorized transactions.

Customers should never approve an authentication request that they did not initiate or do not recognize.

## Protecting Your Account

Customers should use strong, unique passwords for their PixelForge accounts and avoid reusing passwords from other services.

Passwords should not be shared with other people or sent through email or ordinary support messages.

Customers who suspect unauthorized account access should change their password immediately and contact PixelForge support if suspicious orders or account changes are discovered.

For more information about login security and account recovery, see Customer Accounts.

## Recognizing Fraudulent Messages

Fraudulent emails, text messages, and websites may attempt to impersonate online retailers or delivery companies.

Common warning signs include urgent demands for payment, unexpected requests for account credentials, suspicious links, unusual sender addresses, and messages claiming that a delivery cannot proceed without an additional payment.

Customers should avoid opening suspicious links and should navigate directly to the official PixelForge website when checking an order.

PixelForge will never ask customers to disclose their account password or complete payment card security code through an ordinary support email.

## Unexpected Payment Requests

Customers may occasionally receive legitimate payment notifications from an invoice provider or shipping service. However, unexpected requests should always be verified before payment is completed.

PixelForge does not add shipping charges to confirmed orders without the customer's approval.

If a message claims that additional shipping fees must be paid, customers should verify the request through the original order information or contact support.

For details about standard shipping charges, see Shipping Information.

## Suspicious or Unauthorized Transactions

Customers who notice an unfamiliar transaction should contact their bank or payment provider promptly.

The payment provider can explain available procedures for reporting unauthorized card transactions, disputing charges, or protecting the affected payment method.

Customers should also contact PixelForge support if the transaction appears connected to a PixelForge order.

Support may investigate the associated purchase, but PixelForge cannot independently reverse every transaction or make decisions that belong to the payment provider.

## Duplicate Charges

A customer may occasionally see multiple payment entries after an interrupted checkout or repeated payment attempt.

Some entries may represent temporary card authorizations rather than completed charges.

Customers should check whether the transactions are pending or finalized before attempting another purchase.

If two completed charges appear to relate to the same order, customers should contact support with the order number and relevant transaction details.

Customers should not send complete card numbers or security codes when requesting assistance.

## Refund Security

Refunds are normally returned through the original payment method to reduce the risk of fraudulent redirection.

If a customer is asked to provide new banking information for a refund, they should verify the request through an established PixelForge support channel before sharing any details.

PixelForge may require additional identity verification when an alternative refund method is necessary.

For information about refund processing times, see Refund Process.

## Protecting Personal Information

Payment security also involves protecting customer names, addresses, transaction references, and other personal information.

PixelForge limits access to payment-related information according to operational needs and applicable data protection requirements.

Personal information is retained only for appropriate purposes and legal obligations, including relevant accounting requirements.

For information about personal data processing, see Personal Data & GDPR.

## Reporting a Security Concern

Customers who discover suspicious account activity, fraudulent messages, or potential payment security problems should contact PixelForge support.

When reporting an issue, customers should describe what happened and provide relevant order references without sharing passwords or complete payment credentials.

PixelForge may investigate reported security concerns and coordinate with payment providers or other relevant parties when necessary.

title: Troubleshooting Your PC
description: Step-by-step troubleshooting for gaming PCs that fail to start, experience crashes, overheat, or have performance problems.
content:
# Troubleshooting Your PC

Gaming computers contain several interconnected hardware and software components. Problems may occur because of incorrect settings, outdated drivers, incompatible components, overheating, or hardware failures.

This guide explains common troubleshooting procedures that customers can safely perform before contacting PixelForge technical support. The instructions apply primarily to Windows-based gaming PCs, although some recommendations are relevant to other systems.

## Before You Begin Troubleshooting

Before making changes, customers should identify the symptoms and determine when the problem first appeared. Useful information includes whether the problem started after a hardware upgrade, software installation, operating system update, or unexpected shutdown.

Customers should save important files and create backups whenever possible before performing troubleshooting that could affect stored information.

Always shut down the computer and disconnect its power cable before inspecting internal components. Never open a power supply or attempt repairs involving exposed electrical circuitry.

If a computer produces smoke, sparks, a burning smell, or unusual electrical noises, stop using it immediately, disconnect power if safe, and contact support.

## Computer Does Not Turn On

If the computer shows no signs of power, begin by checking the wall outlet, power cable, and power supply switch.

Confirm that the power cable is securely connected to the computer and that the electrical outlet works with another suitable device.

Many desktop power supplies include a physical switch marked I and O. The switch must be in the I position for normal operation.

If the computer is connected through a power strip, try connecting it directly to a functioning wall outlet.

If these checks do not resolve the problem, contact support rather than attempting to open or repair the power supply.

## Computer Turns On but Shows No Display

A computer may power on while the monitor remains black. This can happen because of an incorrect display connection, monitor settings, graphics card problems, or memory initialization issues.

First, verify that the monitor is powered on and that the correct input source is selected.

Check that the HDMI or DisplayPort cable is securely connected at both ends. If the computer has a dedicated graphics card, the monitor should normally be connected to the graphics card rather than the motherboard's display outputs.

Customers may also try another compatible cable or monitor input to rule out a connection problem.

Some motherboards display diagnostic lights or error codes during startup. Customers should record these indicators and consult the motherboard manual before contacting support.

## Windows Fails to Start

If the computer powers on but Windows does not load correctly, the issue may involve corrupted system files, an unsuccessful update, storage problems, or incompatible software.

Customers should record any error messages and note whether Windows displays a recovery screen.

Windows Recovery Environment may provide startup repair and other recovery options. Customers should follow Microsoft's official instructions when using these tools.

Reinstalling Windows can remove applications and may erase personal files depending on the installation method. Customers should not perform a full reset without understanding the consequences and securing important data.

## Unexpected Crashes and Blue Screens

Blue screen errors, sudden restarts, and application crashes may result from driver conflicts, unstable memory settings, overheating, or defective hardware.

Customers should record the error message or stop code shown on the screen. This information can help identify the affected component or software.

If the problem began after a driver update, reverting to a previously working driver may help.

Customers using memory overclocking profiles such as XMP or EXPO may temporarily return the memory to default settings to determine whether the system becomes stable.

BIOS settings should only be changed when the customer understands their purpose. Incorrect settings can prevent a computer from starting normally.

## Overheating and High Fan Noise

Gaming PCs generate heat during demanding applications. Cooling fans may become louder when the processor or graphics card is under heavy load.

However, unusually high temperatures, repeated shutdowns, or severe performance reductions may indicate a cooling problem.

Customers should ensure that ventilation openings are not blocked and that the computer has sufficient space around its intake and exhaust fans.

Dust accumulation can restrict airflow. External vents and accessible dust filters may be cleaned carefully according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Customers should not use liquids inside the computer or interfere with moving fans while the system is powered on.

If overheating continues despite adequate airflow, contact support for further assessment.

## Low Gaming Performance

Poor gaming performance may be caused by demanding graphics settings, background applications, insufficient memory, outdated drivers, or hardware limitations.

Customers should compare the game's recommended system requirements with their computer specifications.

Lowering graphics settings or display resolution may improve performance in demanding games.

Background applications, downloads, and operating system updates can consume system resources. Customers can use Windows Task Manager to identify unusually high processor, memory, or disk usage.

Graphics driver updates may improve compatibility with newer games, but performance improvements vary between applications and hardware configurations.

## Internet and Network Problems

Connection problems may affect multiplayer games, downloads, and online services.

Customers should first determine whether the problem affects only one application or the entire internet connection.

Restarting the router and computer may resolve temporary network problems. Customers should also verify that Wi-Fi or Ethernet connections are active.

For wireless connections, signal strength, interference, and distance from the router may influence stability.

If the problem affects multiple devices, customers may need to contact their internet service provider.

## When to Contact PixelForge Support

Customers should contact support when safe troubleshooting does not resolve the problem, when a hardware defect is suspected, or when the computer displays signs of electrical damage.

Support requests should include the order number, computer model, a description of the symptoms, and any relevant error messages.

Customers should also explain which troubleshooting steps have already been attempted.

For driver installation and operating system guidance, see Driver & Software Support. For possible hardware defects and warranty coverage, consult Warranty Policy.

title: Driver & Software Support
description: Guidance on installing drivers, updating Windows, resolving software conflicts, and maintaining gaming PC stability.
content:
# Driver & Software Support

Drivers and system software allow computer hardware to communicate with the operating system and installed applications. Keeping essential software compatible and reasonably up to date can improve stability, security, and support for newer hardware and games.

This document explains how customers can manage drivers, operating system updates, and common software problems on Windows-based gaming computers.

## What Is a Device Driver?

A device driver is software that enables the operating system to communicate with a hardware component.

Graphics cards, network adapters, audio devices, printers, and many other components require drivers to function correctly.

Windows includes drivers for a wide range of hardware, but some devices benefit from additional software supplied by the manufacturer.

Incorrect, outdated, or incompatible drivers can cause reduced functionality, instability, or unexpected errors.

## Graphics Card Drivers

Graphics drivers are especially important for gaming performance and compatibility with modern games.

Manufacturers such as NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel provide drivers for their supported graphics hardware.

Customers should obtain graphics drivers from official manufacturer websites or trusted update tools supplied by the manufacturer.

New driver versions may include security fixes, bug corrections, and optimizations for specific games. However, updating a driver does not guarantee improved performance in every application.

If a new driver causes problems, customers may need to reinstall a previous stable version following the manufacturer's instructions.

## Motherboard and Chipset Drivers

Chipset drivers help the operating system communicate with important motherboard functions and system controllers.

Depending on the motherboard, additional drivers may be required for networking, audio, wireless connectivity, or other integrated devices.

Customers should identify the exact motherboard model before downloading drivers. Installing software intended for a different motherboard may cause compatibility problems.

Motherboard manufacturers normally provide a support page containing drivers and technical documentation for each model.

## Windows Updates

Windows Update provides operating system security updates, reliability improvements, and some device drivers.

PixelForge recommends keeping supported Windows installations updated, particularly when updates address known security vulnerabilities.

Customers should save open work before installing updates that require a restart.

Some updates may temporarily affect software compatibility. If a problem begins immediately after an update, customers should review the update history and consult official Microsoft support guidance.

## Installing Software Safely

Customers should download applications from official developers, established software stores, or other trustworthy sources.

Unknown download websites may distribute modified installers, unwanted applications, or malicious software.

Customers should be cautious when an installer requests administrator privileges or attempts to install unrelated software.

Antivirus and other security protections should remain enabled unless a trusted troubleshooting procedure specifically requires a temporary change.

## Resolving Software Conflicts

Software conflicts may occur when applications attempt to control the same hardware functions or install incompatible background services.

Examples include multiple RGB lighting utilities, overlapping hardware monitoring tools, or outdated applications that interact with graphics drivers.

Customers experiencing crashes should identify whether the problem occurs in one application or across the entire operating system.

Temporarily disabling recently installed background applications may help identify the cause. Customers should avoid removing essential system services or security software without understanding the consequences.

## BIOS and Firmware Updates

A BIOS or UEFI update may improve hardware compatibility, resolve known issues, or add support for newer processors.

Firmware updates should only be downloaded from the official manufacturer and must match the exact hardware model.

Interrupting a firmware update can make a motherboard or other device unusable. Customers should follow the manufacturer's instructions carefully and ensure a stable power supply during the process.

A BIOS update is not necessary simply because a newer version exists. Customers should review the release notes and determine whether the update addresses a relevant issue.

## Reinstalling Windows

Reinstalling Windows may resolve severe software corruption or persistent operating system problems, but it should generally be considered after less disruptive troubleshooting options.

A reinstall may remove installed applications, custom settings, and personal files depending on the chosen method.

Customers should back up important information before beginning and verify that they have access to necessary installation media, accounts, and software licenses.

PixelForge cannot guarantee recovery of files that were not backed up before a system reset or storage replacement.

## Software Support and Warranty Coverage

PixelForge can provide general assistance with operating system startup, driver installation, and software problems affecting supported hardware.

However, support for third-party applications, game modifications, unsupported operating systems, and individually customized software environments may be limited.

Software problems do not automatically indicate a hardware defect. A warranty assessment may require troubleshooting to determine whether the underlying cause is hardware or software related.

For hardware warranty conditions, see Warranty Policy.

## Preparing Information for Support

When contacting PixelForge about a software issue, customers should provide the computer model, Windows version, affected application, and a description of the symptoms.

Error messages, driver versions, and the approximate time the problem began can also help with diagnosis.

Customers should never send passwords, recovery codes, or other sensitive credentials in ordinary support messages.

For general PC troubleshooting, see Troubleshooting Your PC. For instructions on submitting a support request, consult Contacting Technical Support.

title: Contacting Technical Support
description: How to contact PixelForge support, prepare a support request, understand response times, and follow up on technical issues.
content:
# Contacting Technical Support

PixelForge provides customer support for questions about orders, product compatibility, technical problems, returns, and warranty claims. Our support team aims to help customers identify problems, understand available solutions, and determine when a product requires further inspection.

Providing clear information when submitting a support request helps reduce unnecessary communication and may lead to faster resolution.

## Available Support Channels

Customers can contact PixelForge through the support contact form available on the website or by sending an email to support@pixelforge.example.

The contact form is recommended for technical problems because it allows customers to include order information and a detailed description of the issue.

PixelForge does not currently provide telephone-based technical troubleshooting or live chat with human support agents.

Customers should avoid sending the same request through multiple channels unless additional information is necessary.

## Support Opening Hours

PixelForge customer support operates Monday through Friday, from 09:00 to 17:00 Swedish local time, excluding Swedish public holidays.

Customers may submit requests outside these hours, but responses are normally handled during the next available support period.

Support opening hours do not necessarily correspond to warehouse processing times or shipping provider schedules.

## Expected Response Times

PixelForge aims to provide an initial response to ordinary support requests within two business days.

More complex technical issues, warranty investigations, or cases requiring information from manufacturers may take longer to resolve.

An initial response does not necessarily mean that the entire issue has been resolved. Support may need additional information or testing before recommending a solution.

During periods of unusually high demand, response times may be longer than normal.

## Information to Include in a Support Request

Customers should include their order number when the request concerns a purchase made through PixelForge.

For technical problems, the request should also identify the product model, describe the symptoms, and explain when the issue first occurred.

Useful additional information may include error messages, photographs, hardware specifications, and a list of troubleshooting steps already attempted.

For example, a customer reporting that a gaming PC does not display an image should mention whether the computer powers on, whether the monitor works with another device, and which display connection is being used.

Customers should not include account passwords, payment card security codes, or other sensitive credentials.

## Support for Products Purchased Elsewhere

PixelForge primarily provides technical support for products purchased through our own online store.

Customers who purchased a product from another retailer should normally contact the original seller for assistance with statutory consumer claims.

PixelForge may provide general product information when available, but cannot guarantee troubleshooting, repairs, or warranty administration for purchases made elsewhere.

## Remote Troubleshooting

Some problems can be resolved through written instructions without returning the product.

Support may recommend checking cables, reviewing system settings, installing official drivers, or performing other safe diagnostic procedures.

Customers should only follow troubleshooting instructions they understand and feel comfortable performing.

PixelForge support will not ask customers to disclose their passwords or disable important security protections without a clearly explained and legitimate reason.

If a problem cannot be resolved remotely, the support team may recommend further inspection or a warranty assessment.

## Warranty and Repair Cases

When a hardware defect is suspected, PixelForge may request additional information to determine whether the problem can be resolved through troubleshooting or requires physical inspection.

If a return is necessary, support will provide shipping instructions and explain how the product should be packaged.

For accepted statutory complaints, reasonable return shipping costs are covered according to applicable consumer protection requirements.

Customers should back up personal files before returning computers or storage devices whenever reasonably possible.

For complete information about warranty coverage and statutory complaint rights, see Warranty Policy.

## Following Up on an Existing Case

Customers who have already contacted support should include their existing case reference when sending additional information.

Using the same email conversation or support case helps the support team review previous messages and troubleshooting results.

If the customer has not received an initial response within two business days, they may follow up using the original support channel.

Customers should check their spam folder before submitting a follow-up request.

## Urgent Safety Problems

Customers should immediately stop using a product that produces smoke, sparks, a burning smell, or signs of dangerous electrical failure.

The product should be disconnected from electrical power if this can be done safely.

Customers should not attempt to open or repair damaged power supplies, batteries, or other potentially hazardous electrical components.

If there is an immediate danger to people or property, customers should contact the appropriate emergency services rather than waiting for a support response.

## Questions About Orders and Deliveries

Technical support can also help direct customers to the appropriate information about order processing, delivery delays, missing packages, and cancellations.

Customers seeking information about an existing shipment should provide their order number and tracking number when available.

For delivery estimates, see Delivery Times. For shipment status information, see Order Tracking. For cancellation requests, consult Cancelling an Order.

## Privacy and Support Correspondence

PixelForge processes personal information provided in support requests for the purpose of handling customer inquiries and fulfilling relevant legal obligations.

Support correspondence may contain order references, contact details, and technical information about the affected product.

Customers should avoid including unnecessary personal information and should remove sensitive files or credentials from attachments.

For information about personal data processing and customer rights, see Personal Data & GDPR.
